text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein says Washington summit was "neither a total failure nor a complete success"; emphasises "that peace will prevail..and what is important is continuing negotiations from the point they stopped."
- The influential Islamic Action Front (IAF) condemns the Washington summit and calls on Arabs and Moslems to save Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.
- Pakistani army chief of staff arrives in Jordan on an official visit.
- Customs officials say there is no intention to further reduce tariffs on cars because current tariffs are "realistic and fair."
- A new draft law on brand names and trademarks to prevent forgeries and reduce bureacratic red tape.
- King Hussein, in live interviews with U.S. television networks, says Washington summit helped create "the right climate" and calls for implementing peace accords.
- Prime Minister Kabariti returns home to Amman on Sunday after attending the Washington summit.
- Information Minister Muasher says overcoming the crisis requires Israel's implementation of the peace accords.

- King says disaster was the situation before the Washington summit; "at stake was the entire future of the quest for peace". Jordan disappointed by Israeli failure to inform it of Jerusalem tunnel opening.
- A seminar to be organised to discuss plans to privatise state television and state media organs.
- Discussions on allowing private sector imports of salt, currently a state monopoly.
